title: The Lion and the Clever Hare
text:
In a forest lived a mighty lion named Bhasuraka who killed animals without end, far more than he could eat. At last the animals went to him with a proposal. If he would stay in his den, they would send him one animal every day for his meal. He agreed, and from then on the animals drew lots each day to choose who would go.

One day the lot fell to a hare. He knew he was going to die, but he took his time on the way, thinking hard. He arrived very late, and the lion, starving and angry, roared at him.

The hare bowed and explained. Other hares had set out with him, he said, but on the way another lion had stopped them, claimed the forest as his own, and eaten his companions. He alone had been allowed to go and report.

Bhasuraka was enraged. He demanded to be shown this rival at once. The hare led him to a deep well and pointed down. The lion looked in and saw a lion glaring up at him from the water. He roared, and the well roared back. In his fury he leaped down to attack the rival and drowned. The hare went home and told the animals they were free.
lesson: A more powerful opponent can often be beaten through his own pride and temper. Find what he cannot resist reacting to, and let him defeat himself.
